page.title: Coverage
page.purpose: Show the cell grid as it actually is — every projection, every cell, its status, the bar it is graded against, and the confidence of the space it was measured against. Every open-loop cell carries the date it was declared and how long it has stood.

regions.purpose: The primary object on the page: projections down, cells across, each showing NOW / IN-REACH / MISSING with its bar and honesty flag.
Per-projection denominator-confidence with its rationale, presented beside the ratio it qualifies rather than in a tooltip.
Separate the MISSING cells, each with gap_opened_on and gap_open_days, so an intentionally visible hole can be told from an overdue one.

Report setpoint-integrity findings — a NOW cell with no bar, a bar equal to its authoring-time reading, a hand-set honesty flag — and drift findings where a named sensor no longer resolves or a MISSING cell could already be closed by a shipped verb.

states.description: Spaces read, setpoint parsed, grid joined. Cells, confidence, open-loop and integrity findings all shown.

One owner's space verb could not be read. That projection shows UNAVAILABLE with the reason and SKETCH confidence; its cells keep their last authored status and none is fabricated as MISSING. Other projections render normally.
The setpoint parses but one or more bars are malformed. The grid still loads; the malformed entries are called out rather than dropped.
The setpoint file is missing, unreadable or unparseable. A hard, loud failure — no cell count is shown.
Coverage spaces and setpoint are loading.
Some owner spaces are unavailable while other projections remain readable.
The coverage request failed and the failure is named.
The last coverage snapshot remains visible while refresh is pending.
No coverage cells are available yet; this is distinct from a passing measured grid.

priorities.statement: The setpoint is read-only here, and the page must look it.
priorities.notes: No edit affordance of any kind. Changing a bar is an operator decision made through a reliability-target-update in a reviewed commit, not a UI action. An edit control here would be deviation D6 rendered in pixels, and this page is the single most likely place for that boundary to be eroded by a well-meaning addition.

priorities.statement: An open-loop cell is presented as a declared state, not as missing data.
priorities.notes: MISSING cells are honest declarations of blindness. They are counted and dated, never hidden and never shown as a failure of the plant.

priorities.statement: No ratio appears without its denominator-confidence.
priorities.notes: A coverage percentage published without the confidence of the space it was measured against implies a completeness the board has not earned.

claims.statement: The page exposes no control that would create, edit or delete a projection, cell, bar, deadband or actuator.
claims.rationale: The instrument may not author either half of its own denominator. There is deliberately no API path to call even if a control were added.

claims.statement: Every coverage ratio is rendered adjacent to its denominator-confidence level and rationale, in the same visual unit.
claims.rationale: Recursive honesty is the property that keeps a SKETCH denominator from reading as an authoritative one. Relegating it to a tooltip defeats it.

claims.statement: Every MISSING cell displays the date its gap was declared and the number of days it has stood.
claims.rationale: Without the dates, 'declared and dated' degrades into 'declared once and forgotten' — the state three framework-health targets sat in indefinitely.

claims.statement: When an owner's space cannot be read, its cells retain their authored status and are visibly marked UNAVAILABLE with the reason; none is rendered as MISSING or as 0%.
claims.rationale: An owner outage reading as a coverage collapse would make every board reading untrustworthy during exactly the incidents the board exists to surface.

claims.statement: When the setpoint cannot be parsed, the page states the failure and its reason and shows no cell count.
claims.rationale: An empty grid rendered as zero cells would read as a scenario with nothing to measure rather than an instrument that lost its reference.
